title: SLO Guardian: Config Operator for Safe Batch/Cache Optimizations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight operator (SLO Guardian) that applies batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations automatically while enforcing latency and throughput guardrails. The operator must be able to stage changes, detect anomalies during rollouts, pause and rollback safely, and emit rich signals for the Console and alerting. This reduces manual tuning work and keeps user-facing SLOs intact during cost-optimization campaigns.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can apply recommended batching/cache profiles to a canary subset of traffic (configurable %).
Operator evaluates latency P95 and throughput against configured SLO thresholds and pauses or rolls back on breach within rollout window.
Anomaly detector flags significant deviations within 5 minutes and annotates the rollout event in Console audit logs.
Rollback is automated and completes within SLA for affected tenants (target: <30s to route to previous config after detection).
Operator emits metrics and traces compatible with Console dashboards and existing SLO alerting (mTLS + prometheus-compatible endpoints).
E2E tests and chaos scenarios for partial networking failures and delayed KV-cache priming included in CI.
Design doc, GH PR, and runbook created and reviewed by Reliability and Product teams.
implementation_notes: Design will be a control-loop component in the runtime control plane that subscribes to cost-optimizer recommendations and applies diffs as staged patches.
Staging model: shadow -> canary (X% traffic) -> ramp -> full. Default canary = 2% but configurable per-customer and per-model.
Guardrails: P95 latency SLA, error-rate threshold, and throughput floor. Each guardrail has soft and hard thresholds; soft triggers slow ramp, hard triggers immediate rollback.
Anomaly detection: combine EWMA of P95 and a magnitude test against baseline distribution. Use both relative and absolute checks to avoid sensitivity to noise on low-traffic routes.
Limiters: global concurrency limiter, per-route in-flight caps, and adaptive micro-window backoff to prevent cascading latency spikes.
Rollback strategy: two-phase rollback — immediate route fallback + background garbage-collection of applied config to avoid re-apply on flapping recommendations.
Safety: idempotent config application, optimistic locking on config versions, and an allowlist for customers who opt out of automated applies.
Telemetry: annotate rollout events with recommendation_id, operator_run_id, metrics snapshot, and detected_anomalies for correlation in Console.
Security: operator runs with minimal RBAC scope; audit logs for every config mutation and rollback.
work_plan: Week 1: Finalize design doc and API contract with Console and Optimizer teams. Deliverable: design doc + sequence diagram.
Week 2: Implement control-loop skeleton, config diff applier, and versioning primitives. Deliverable: internal feature branch.
Week 3: Integrate simple anomaly detector and gating logic. Add prometheus metrics and tracing points. Deliverable: demo with synthetic traffic.
Week 4: End-to-end canary flow, rollback handlers, and console event annotations. Deliverable: QA runbook and initial e2e tests.
Week 5: Chaos scenarios, performance testing at scale, and security review. Deliverable: runbook update and pre-release checklist.
Week 6: Gradual rollout to non-critical tenants with monitoring and on-call playbook. Deliverable: production pilot and postmortem.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from anomaly detector cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require sustained breach over configurable window before rollback; use soft gates to slow ramp first.
Risk: KV-cache priming latency causes transient spikes on canaries. Mitigation: prefetch common prefixes for canary traffic and include warm-up stage in rollout choreography.
Risk: Config flapping between optimizer runs. Mitigation: implement cooldown period and garbage collection of superseded recommendations.
Risk: Operator bug affects many customers. Mitigation: start with opt-in pilot tenants and allowlist; provide instant global kill-switch and manual review paths.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for config diff and idempotency logic.
Integration tests for canary routing and fallback correctness using test runtime clusters.
E2E test harness that injects synthetic latency and error modes to validate anomaly triggers and rollback timing.
Load test verifying operator latency overhead is <2% of control-plane p99 for 99th percentile of simultaneous rollouts.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: rollout_success_rate, rollback_count, time_to_rollback_seconds, canary_p95_delta, canary_error_rate_delta, operator_cpu_ms.
Alerting rules: high rollback_count (>3 in 10m), canary_p95_delta > 2x SLO for >5m, operator_error_rate > 1%.
Console dashboard: per-model rollout map, live canary health heatmap, and annotated timeline for recommendations.
Post-incident telemetry retention: snapshot recommended configuration, metric baselines, and traces for 24h after any automated rollback.
